channel.title: MCP Monitor Daily Report
channel.description: Daily monitoring of Model Context Protocol mentions

item.title: Anthropic is turning MCP into more than a tool bus - PaPoo
item.description: A bug in an agent orchestration harness lets strangers run commands on your machine without asking nicely. Your AI's memory is apparently fair game too.

item.title: GitHub - Heming9/agenterm: Let agents control any remote computer, anytime, anywhere. Self-hosted AI agent remote assistance via MCP and terminal. · GitHub
item.description: Agents get a remote terminal and a polite invitation link, so helping grandma with her printer finally becomes something your AI can do from its own chat window.

item.title: Submit a project · SilentStars
item.description: A directory for quietly shipping open-source projects, where a bot decides who gets in. A couple of the picks happen to speak MCP.

item.title: Google Workspace Updates: Simplifying agent access while keeping organizations in control: MCP servers, CLI, standardized usage tiers, and admin policies
item.description: Google has decided that AI agents should talk to Workspace through MCP or get nowhere near the REST APIs, and it has the usage tiers and admin controls to make that stick.

item.title: MCP 2주년, 클로드에서 Skills over MCP 공개 베타·Tasks와 Elicitation 정식 지원
item.description: MCP turned two, and it brought gifts: skills you can ship from a server, long jobs that run in the background, and a polite way to ask a human before deleting your repo.

item.title: MysticAPI - Human Design & astrology engine API
item.description: Astrology meets AI plumbing: a chart engine that skips the vibes and ships a remote MCP server so your model can read your Energy Blueprint on demand.

item.title: Adchestra - Run Google Ads from your AI
item.description: Your AI agent can now run your Google Ads account, which is either a productivity miracle or a very expensive way to learn what a bad keyword costs.

item.title: Usage tiers and quotas for Google Workspace APIs and MCP servers | Google for Developers
item.description: Google has decided that AI agents should talk to Workspace through MCP rather than raw REST calls, and it's putting a price tag and a quota on the privilege.

item.title: GitHub - cerulion-inc/cerulion: Cerulion (YC S24) gives AI agents a harness to control real robots. Our open-source runtime and harness give any AI agent a physical body, inside safety limits the robot enforces, and tools to autonomously debug recorded robot failures. It's ROS 2 compatible. · GitHub
item.description: Turns out giving a language model an MCP server is a pretty reasonable way to hand it a robot arm, provided you also record everything so you can replay the mistakes.

item.title: ruflo の MCP ブリッジに認証なし RCE、CVE-2026-59726 | テック注意報
item.description: Turns out an MCP bridge with no login and wide-open ports is an open invitation. Update ruflo to 3.16.3 and rotate your API keys if you ran the default setup.

item.title: GitHub - wakeshift/server: Wakeshift lets an MCP server wake the AI agents that use it. The open-source server delivers MCP Events per the spec and wakes agents that can't subscribe yet. Run it yourself or use the hosted service. · GitHub
item.description: Your MCP server has news, but Claude Code and friends are asleep at the wheel. This server gives them a nudge, politely, through a webhook or a background wait.

item.title: Introducing mcpdiff.dev: Devtools for MCP | from the trenches
item.description: MCP has changed five times in two years, so keeping the spec in your head is a lost cause. Here's a browser tool that does the reading for you, sequence diagrams included.

item.title: Anthropic's MCP Protocol Hits 700M Downloads
item.description: Seven hundred million downloads later, the little protocol that lets language models reach outside their own heads is apparently not so little anymore.

item.title: Use Chrome DevTools MCP Logpoints Without Editing | Dirty Static
item.description: Printf debugging, but the printf lives in the browser and your source file never gets dirty. Chrome DevTools MCP now lets your coding agent do the logging for you.

item.title: Two years of MCP: the vibe and the volume | Runlayer
item.description: MCP was declared dead roughly as often as it was declared the future, and the download charts kept climbing through both. Here is the whole soap opera on one page.

item.title: How the agent-ready score works · BOTERNITY
item.description: Turns out your website can be graded on how friendly it is to robots that don't have eyeballs. Announce your MCP server and collect points, block everything and get an F.

item.title: Add the Microsoft Learn MCP server for .NET in Claude Code
item.description: Claude Code knows .NET 9 far better than .NET 11, so the author plugged in a documentation server and asked it to write union types. Then they tried again without it and watched what happened.

item.title: Connect ngrok MCP Server To Coding Agents | Dirty Static
item.description: Your coding agent can finally see your ngrok account, live endpoints and all, but it acts with your permissions, so read every change request before you approve it.

item.title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude | Claude by Anthropic
item.description: Turns out MCP servers have learned some manners: they can now hand Claude a playbook, go off and work in the background, and politely ask before doing anything destructive.

item.title: Two Years of MCP Builders | Model Context Protocol Blog
item.description: Two years in, the protocol that started as a side project has more downloads than most of us have had hot dinners, and a robot desk buddy to show for it.

item.title: gMCP: A Self-Hosted MCP For Google Tag Manager & Your Google Data
item.description: Talking to your analytics stack through a language model sounds tidy until you start wondering where your tokens end up. This guide walks through building one MCP server to rule them all.

item.title: GitHub - lyriks-io/lyriks-community: Lyriks Community edition: the open-source product-specification platform (SvelteKit, PostgreSQL, MCP) · GitHub
item.description: Your code knows what it does, but nobody remembers why. Lyriks lets your AI assistant write that down through MCP, so the spec finally keeps up with the code.

item.title: GitHub - Suncly-Tech/mcp-reliability-index: Independent, pre-registered check of whether popular MCP servers' tools do what they say. · GitHub
item.description: Turns out a tool's own description is a promise, and someone is now checking whether the promises hold. Release 1 reads declarations only, Release 2 actually tests read-only tools.

item.title: GitHub - ranadhir19/mcp-server-lab: Build an MCP server a model can actually use - two server designs measured head-to-head: strict schemas, an independent audit, and 32 graded trials. Companion lab to The Architect's AI Workshop, Agent Series Episode 1. · GitHub
item.description: Models never see your server code, only tool names and schemas, so this lab tests whether a stricter schema actually makes a small model pick the right tool more often.

item.title: Best Video and YouTube MCP servers (November 2026) · tested every night
item.description: A leaderboard for video MCP servers, re-tested every night from the outside, where most entries score well but a surprising number of contenders are just the same server listed under different names.

item.title: GitHub - dorgrn/decloak: Find instructions hidden in AI agent skills, rules files and MCP servers · GitHub
item.description: Hidden prompts in your agent's config files are the new malware, and this tool digs them out offline, no LLM required. Your MCP servers have nothing to hide, presumably.

item.title: Openhood: the free car fault reader
item.description: Your car's engine light has finally met its match: a free browser tool that translates cryptic codes into plain words, and optionally hands the diagnosis to your AI.

item.title: GitHub - olgaysezgin/autologin-mcp: Auto-login MCP for AI coding agents. Logs your agent into the app under test; credentials stay on your machine and never reach the model. · GitHub
item.description: Teaching your AI agent to log in without handing it the keys: a small MCP server that fills login forms locally, so the password stays out of the chat.

item.title: Agent-ready leaderboard: how websites welcome AI agents · BOTERNITY
item.description: Turns out most websites still greet AI agents at the door with a frown. A public leaderboard tracks who is actually rolling out the welcome mat.

item.title: The first AI-ready OS installer | Agama
item.description: Your operating system installer now wants to chat with your AI assistant. Agama adds an MCP server, with guardrails firmly in place so the robot doesn't format the wrong disk.

item.title: Build your own AI agent that finds and messages other agents · LobsterMatch
item.description: Teaching an agent to talk to other agents, one signed webhook at a time, with nothing but the standard library and a healthy respect for not waking the model needlessly.

item.title: Tool catalog: direct tools and platform routers | AdAce Ads
item.description: Turns out your ads dashboard can now be chatted with, provided you remember which operations are the dangerous ones. The catalog spells that out.

item.title: BOTERNITY log, 2026-11-23
item.description: Turns out most public MCP servers are either wide open, locked behind a login, or quietly broken. The registry is growing faster than anyone is checking it.

item.title: GitHub - aplaceforallmystuff/mcp-arr: MCP server for *arr media management suite · GitHub
item.description: Your media library, now answering to plain English. This MCP server gives your *arr stack a single tool interface that Claude and ChatGPT can actually use, with the guardrails to match.

item.title: Benchline: free browser tools for web work · Benchline
item.description: Eighty-two browser tools walk into an endpoint and come out as something your AI assistant can actually use. Paste one URL and stop guessing what a web page wants.

item.title: Before you publish an MCP server: a checklist for stdio and for secrets - ZEUS LAB
item.description: Before an MCP server meets the public internet, one stray print statement can break the whole session, and a committed API key can break much more. Here is the seven-point checklist.

item.title: @hashshabbir/mcp-pack - npm
item.description: Twenty tiny MCP connectors walk into a package registry, and one of them checks the others for trouble before you let them near your keys.

item.title: microfeed documentation | microfeed docs
item.description: Your blog, minus the server babysitting. Microfeed lets your favourite AI assistant poke at your content through MCP, which is either delightful or a reason to double-check your permissions.

item.title: Superlinear Academy 注目投稿：オフライン地図、出典付きAPI、イベント運営の学び
item.description: A single offline HTML map, a data server that actually admits where its answers came from, and a podcast on running events with 1600 attendees. Practical stuff, mostly.
